newsitem.title: PERU: Most wanted drug baron flown from Ecuador to Peru.
newsitem.headline: Most wanted drug baron flown from Ecuador to Peru.

text.p: Peru's most wanted drug trafficker was flown home under heavy police escort on Tuesday from neighbouring Ecuador where he was captured on Sunday.
Willer Alvarado Linares was expected to stand trial for running a drug ring that supplied cocaine paste to Colombia's Cali cartel and for working with leftist guerrillas in Peru.
President Alberto Fujimori said the capture of Alvarado and more than 40 members of his gang in Peru and Ecuador was "one of the biggest blows against drug-trafficking in recent times."
A Peruvian air force plane flew Alvarado and four associates from Quito to Lima where they were taken to Peru's anti-drug police headquarters.

Peruvian authorities said Alvarado was the most powerful Peruvian drug lord at large who controlled the sale of coca leaves, the raw material for making cocaine, in the Amazonian regions near the Colombian border.
Police said Alvarado supplied up to four tonnes of cocaine paste a month to the Cali cartel.
Police also wanted Alvarado arrested for collaborating with Maoist guerrillas, whom he allegedly paid to guard his drug operations.

Intelligence sources said Alvarado's capture followed a tip-off by a rival band seeking to take over his drug trade in Aucayacu in central Peru. A joint operation by Ecuadoran, Peruvian and Colombian police caught him five months later.
Eight people died on Sunday in fighting between the two drug gangs trying to control the drug-growing jungle region around Aucayacu, police said.
